title: EIP-7928: Block-Level Access Lists (Last Call, deadline 2026-11-01)
quote: block_access_list_hash ... For an empty block access list, this is keccak256(rlp.encode([])) = 0x1dcc4de8dec75d7aab85b567b6ccd41ad312451b948a7413f0a142fd40d49347. ... The BlockAccessList is not included in the block body. ... bal_items <= block_gas_limit // ITEM_COST ... ITEM_COST = 2000 ... buffer of approximately block_gas_limit / 42000 extra items ... A storage key MUST NOT appear in both storage_changes and storage_reads for the same account. ... The EL MUST retain BALs for at least the duration of the weak subjectivity period (3533 epochs) ... def track_state_changes ... for slot in get_storage_reads(addr): if slot not in accesses[addr]['storage_writes']: accesses[addr]['storage_reads'].add(slot) ... The BAL MUST be complete and accurate. Missing or spurious entries invalidate the block. ... A malicious proposer could exploit this by declaring spurious storage reads that are never accessed ... The bal_items constraint bounds the number of such entries.

title: Ethereum Magicians — EIP-7928 discussion thread
quote: (35 posts, 2025-04-01 to 2025-12-02.) dajuguan: "After introducing BAL, Geth's live sync performance improved by approximately 30%" (addresses and keys only, no diffs). raul: "At 40KiB, this represents a non-negligible overhead that causes block sizes to increase by 2x, and p95 grows by 1.55x ... I propose exploring whether we can replace the diff traces ... with a deterministic, canonical, parallelizable tx execution plan". Nerolation: "it lacks a key feature: executionless state updates ... we can no longer use this data for purposes like syncing"; "even if a block contains transactions that depend on one another in sequence, we can achieve the same level of parallelization as if all transactions were completely independent." Raycoms proposed dependency-only hints; Nerolation: "it doesn't help in worst-cases". benaadams proposed XOR byte diffs to improve compression.

title: ethereum/EIPs PR #12347 — Update EIP-7928: align BAL retention with the history expiry window
quote: Opened 2026-09-16 by nflaig, open as of 2026-10-19. "Block access lists only have to be retained for 3,533 epochs, the weak subjectivity period at a safety decay of 10, but consensus clients must serve execution payloads for 14,299 epochs ... the block access list is the one payload field left outside it: once pruned, engine_getPayloadBodiesBy*V2 returns null for it and the payload can no longer be rebuilt." Diff: "+The EL MUST keep BALs available via engine_getPayloadBodiesBy*V2 for at least HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS (=14299 epochs)". LukaszRozmej: "BAL is just optimisation structure, node can validate block without BAL's, thus we don't really need big retention window for it." nflaig: "this is not about what the EL needs, the problem is that the CL needs to serve blocks and payloads".

title: ethereum/EIPs PR #12546 — Update EIP-8159: follow the EIP-7928 BAL retention change
quote: Opened 2026-10-19 by nerolation: "Follow-up to #12347, which aligns BAL retention in EIP-7928 with HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS, the block body retention window."
